name: The Promise Ring
label: Jade Tree
lede: Four Milwaukee kids turned emo into power pop and nearly died doing it: a van through a windshield in a Nebraska snowstorm, a brain tumor found the day a tour was due to leave, and a last album made to get away from the word emo.

eras.title: Borrowed from Cap'n Jazz
eras.text: The Promise Ring came out of two dead Milwaukee bands and a guitarist loaned from Chicago's Cap'n Jazz. Within months that loan became permanent, because Cap'n Jazz broke up on the road.

years.h: The Promise Ring forms from two broken Milwaukee bands
years.p: Guitarists [[Jason Gnewikow|d6ee8d9d-ef4a-4f96-8e7a-bf5f239c2ac0]] and Matt Mangan of None Left Standing join drummer [[Dan Didier|60e8d768-3d24-446b-b21c-1dffc6fbca7b]] and bassist Scott Beschta of Ceilishrine in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

years.h: Matt Mangan moves away; Davey von Bohlen of Cap'n Jazz steps in
years.p: Matt Mangan relocates to Indianapolis. Jason Gnewikow's friend [[Davey von Bohlen|b1bb1a6c-898b-4d0d-ab0a-6473859d229b]], guitarist in [[Cap'n Jazz|04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825]], takes his place.

years.h: The first Promise Ring demo: Jupiter, 12 Sweaters Red, Mineral Point
years.p: The new line-up records a three-song demo. Mineral Point and Watertown Plank soon come out on a 7-inch on Foresight Records, a friend's label.

years.h: Cap'n Jazz breaks up on tour, so Davey von Bohlen comes home
years.p: After a ten-day Promise Ring run on the East Coast, von Bohlen heads out with [[Cap'n Jazz|04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825]]. That band splits on the ninth day of its tour, and he's a full-time Promise Ring member from then on.

eras.title: A tape handed to Jade Tree
eras.text: A demo passed along by a friend in Texas Is the Reason got The Promise Ring a three-album deal with Jade Tree, a Delaware label known for hardcore. The band hated its first album, and fans made it an emo standard anyway.

years.h: Norman Brannon hands The Promise Ring's tape to Jade Tree
years.p: [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]] guitarist [[Norman Brannon|fbe11657-2638-4486-8369-2157644a9031]] gives the demo and 7-inch to Jade Tree co-founder Tim Owen. Owen signs the band to a three-album contract.

years.h: Falsetto Keeps Time EP
years.p: The Promise Ring's first Jade Tree release, while the band keeps playing church halls and basements across the US.

years.h: Split single with Texas Is the Reason
years.p: The Promise Ring shares a split single with [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]], the band whose guitarist got them signed.

q: The wrong recording at the wrong time with the wrong person.
years.h: 30° Everywhere: five days, a sick singer, an emo staple
years.p: Cut in five days in June 1996 at Idful Music with engineer [[Casey Rice|ea30cea0-fb0c-4893-835d-1629e8c1dff3]], while Davey von Bohlen was ill. It had sold 12,000 copies by September 1997, and A Picture Postcard became an emo standard.
years.xp:
The band was hard on it. Davey von Bohlen said he'd never listen to the first record, and said they had no idea what they wanted it to sound like.

Fans disagreed. 30° Everywhere made LA Weekly's list of the 20 best emo albums.

years.h: Six weeks on the road with Texas Is the Reason
years.p: The Promise Ring tours the US for six weeks with [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]], then does Europe in April and May 1997.

years.h: Scott Beschta is out after clashing with Dan Didier
years.p: Beschta and Didier fell out during the sessions for the second album. Tim Burton, Jason Gnewikow's old None Left Standing bandmate, takes bass for the tour.

years.h: Nothing Feels Good, cut in Memphis with J. Robbins
years.p: Recorded in June 1997 at Easley McCain in Memphis with [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]], it sold in the mid five figures and made best-of lists in the New York Times and Teen People.
years.xp: The sound got poppier without losing the emo core. Darren Doane directed the Why Did Ever We Meet video. The cover photo was shot in front of Trimper's Rides on the boardwalk in Ocean City, Maryland.

eras.title: A windshield and a brain tumor
eras.text: At its peak The Promise Ring was nearly wiped out twice. A van wreck put the singer through the windshield and the guitarist in intensive care. Two years later a brain tumor behind 18 months of onstage headaches cancelled a tour on departure day.

years.h: The Promise Ring's van flips in a Nebraska snowstorm
years.p: On tour with [[Hum|04c5ca8a-4afa-4031-aced-6357440dbc25]], Davey von Bohlen hits a bump and the van rolls. Von Bohlen goes head-first through the windshield. Jason Gnewikow spends three weeks in intensive care.
years.xp:
Von Bohlen had head trauma. Bassist Tim Burton broke bones, and Gnewikow's injuries included a broken collarbone. Dan Didier was released from hospital the next morning.

The band took six weeks to recover before playing again.

years.h: Scott Schoenbeck replaces Tim Burton after the crash
years.p: With Schoenbeck on bass, The Promise Ring returns on the East Coast with [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]], then tours Europe that summer with [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]].

years.h: Boys + Girls EP
years.p: The Promise Ring's stopgap EP carries Tell Everyone We're Dead and Best Looking Boys.

years.h: Davey von Bohlen and Dan Didier start Vermont
years.p: The two start Vermont, an acoustic side project with Chris Rosenau of [[Pele|eb54e2fe-5477-42ed-a976-f242e51c2895]].

years.h: Very Emergency: power pop from J. Robbins' house
years.p: The band stayed at [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]]' home in Silver Spring, Maryland, and recorded at Inner Ear in Washington, D.C. It came out the same day as [[The Get Up Kids|1b54e90c-638e-4fdd-a20e-4ab09db9fdaf]]' Something to Write Home About.
years.xp:
[[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]] and Hilary Soldati of Smart Went Crazy guest. The Emergency! Emergency! video, directed by Darren Doane, premiered on MTV's 120 Minutes in October. Spin put the album among the top 20 releases of 1999.

That fall The Promise Ring toured the US with Robbins' band [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]], joined on dates by [[Pele|eb54e2fe-5477-42ed-a976-f242e51c2895]] and [[The Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]].

years.h: Davey von Bohlen's brain tumor cancels The Promise Ring's Europe tour
years.p: On the day the band was due to leave for Europe with [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]], von Bohlen is diagnosed with a meningioma. He has surgery on May 8.
years.xp:
He had been getting intense headaches during shows for 18 months. The operation involved removing and reattaching part of his skull. The Electric Pink EP, two Very Emergency outtakes, came out that month.

The band came back in September supporting [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]] for three weeks, but a post-operative infection forced them off the tour.

years.h: Davey von Bohlen sings on Jimmy Eat World's A Praise Chorus
years.p: Von Bohlen guests on A Praise Chorus by [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]], friends from the road. The song became a promotional single from Bleed American.

eras.title: Out of emo, and out
eras.text: The Promise Ring left Jade Tree for Epitaph's new Anti- imprint and made a Stephen Street record to get away from the scene it had helped build. The sessions cost them a bassist and von Bohlen fainted at SXSW. Six months after the album came out, the band was done.

years.h: The Promise Ring leaves Jade Tree for Epitaph's Anti-
years.p: The Promise Ring splits from Jade Tree, which couldn't give the financial backing the band wanted. After courting from Epitaph Records, it signs to the Anti- imprint.
years.xp: Part of the move was the word itself. On Jade Tree the band had become more and more identified as emo, and it wanted distance from that. For shows with Camden that spring, Camden's William Seidel joined on keyboards.

years.h: Stephen Street vanishes on vacation; Scott Schoenbeck quits
years.p: [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]] producer [[Stephen Street|47c7deb5-2e24-45ec-944e-d9d103afb312]] goes on vacation mid-project and can't be reached. Schoenbeck, unhappy with the new direction, leaves during the LA sessions and Camden's Ryan Weber takes over.
years.xp: With the budget in trouble, the band split Wood/Water between Street at Jacobs Studios in Farnham, England, and [[Mario Caldato Jr.|92762a95-0762-4604-b5bf-0d4ff3961de3]] in Los Angeles, who produced Say Goodbye Good.

years.h: Davey von Bohlen faints at SXSW, then more surgery
years.p: Von Bohlen collapses at South by Southwest and has another operation, which leaves a plate in his head.

years.h: Wood/Water · Anti-, and a Stephen Street sound
years.p: The Promise Ring's fourth album trades emo for a softer, stranger pop record. The Stop Playing Guitar video was directed by ex-[[GusGus|f5cff7b2-b19d-4934-8525-b17248b30ab3]] members Arni + Kinski.

years.h: The Promise Ring plays Late Night with Conan O'Brien
years.p: Mid-way through a US tour with [[The Weakerthans|bc68928b-fbb5-4aac-baae-52ba49202372]], the band plays network TV, then heads to the UK supporting [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]].

years.h: Epitaph announces The Promise Ring's breakup
years.p: After closing out the Plea for Peace tour, the band calls it a day. The members said they'd been thinking about it for months, and a planned video for Suffer Never was never filmed.

eras.title: Maritime, and a few Metro nights
eras.text: Von Bohlen and Didier kept playing together as Maritime. The Promise Ring came back for occasional nights, mostly at Chicago's Metro, but ruled out new music.

years.h: Davey von Bohlen and Dan Didier start In English, later Maritime
years.p: With [[Eric Axelson|ecc42a4f-e214-40f1-af6d-6cdcade19702]] of [[The Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]] they form In English, soon renamed [[Maritime|dbc59d71-6d29-4563-ba89-a60bab1c0f40]]. Anti- passed on the debut, Glass Floor, which DeSoto released in 2004.

years.h: A one-off at Metro's Flower 15 festival
years.p: The Promise Ring plays a single reunion set at the Flower 15 Festival at Metro in Chicago.

q: No interest at all to write new music.
years.h: Reunion shows, but no new songs
years.p: After a November 2011 tweet, The Promise Ring plays reunion shows and then Bamboozle, Riot Fest and Fun Fun Fun Fest. A rarities set promised for Dangerbird Records never appeared.

years.h: Nothing Feels Good in full at Metro on New Year's Eve
years.p: The Promise Ring plays all of Nothing Feels Good at Metro Chicago. Dan Didier: maybe more shows, but definitely not new music.

years.h: Wrecking Ball festival, The Promise Ring's last documented show
years.p: The band plays the Wrecking Ball festival, its last documented live appearance.
